fieldMarks: Butterscotch-coloured with a gray bill, long neck and white stripes on the flanks
In flight, black underwings and a white crescent above the tail contrast with the buff body
behavior: Regular migration by some Gulf Coast birds to southern Mexico, overshadowed by widespread wandering; flocks have strayed to at least six Canadian provinces
Feeds in water by dabbling or tipping up, sometimes diving; much foraging in damp fields, especially rice fields
Diet more than 95% plant material, mainly seeds of aquatic plants and grasses
habitat: Fresh or brackish marshes in flat open country of the coastal plain, flooded rice fields, other agricultural fields, ponds and lakes.
range: Breeds in southern California, southwestern Arizona, central and eastern Texas, Gulf Coast Louisiana and locally southern Florida, south to central Mexico; also breeds in Hawaii (Oahu) and in South America, Africa and India. Spread east along the Gulf Coast from about 1950.

lookalikes.name: Black-bellied whistling-duck (young)
lookalikes.howToTell: Audubon says to compare young Black-bellied with Fulvous; Fulvous is uniformly butterscotch with a gray bill and white flank stripes.

lookalikes.name: Northern pintail (female)
lookalikes.howToTell: Audubon lists female Northern Pintail for comparison; Fulvous has a long neck, white flank stripes and the white rump crescent.
